"""Tiny synthetic catalog package used by the memory effect benchmark."""


def slugify(label: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase slug. Historical investigation found punctuation remains."""
    return "-".join(label.strip().lower().split())
"""Synthetic archive key module, related to catalog labels but independently used."""


def archive_key(title: str) -> str:
    return "_".join(title.strip().lower().split())
"""Feed ingestion delegates its durable key to catalog.slugify."""
from catalog import slugify


def import_record(title: str, records: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    key = slugify(title)
    records[key] = title
    return key
"""Lookups use the archive key formatter, independently of ingestion."""
from archive import archive_key


def lookup_record(title: str, records: dict[str, str]) -> str | None:
    return records.get(archive_key(title))
"""Current import policy. This file is authoritative for the stale control."""

item.text: Both formatters now extract lowercase ASCII alphanumeric runs and join them with underscores, so import and lookup produce the same key. I’ve added formatter and end-to-end regression coverage; I’m running the requested unittest discovery now.
